evals.prompt: Use the official Bun Guide structure to explain when Bun is a good fit for a Go REST API backend, then provide a quick-start style example with a User model, database bootstrap, insert, and select.
evals.expected_output: Follows the official Key Features, Quick Start, How Bun Works, and Common Use Cases chapters; keeps Bun SQL-first and shows bootstrap plus basic insert/select code.

assertions.text: The output explicitly frames Bun as SQL-first and built on database/sql.
The output includes a quick-start style model plus NewInsert and NewSelect examples.
The output references REST API backend use without putting query-builder code directly in controllers.

evals.prompt: Following the official Bun Guide Query Building Examples chapter, show CRUD plus an advanced reporting query with a join or relation, a subquery, aggregation, grouping, and a DTO scan struct.
evals.expected_output: Uses official query-building patterns: NewInsert, NewSelect, NewUpdate, NewDelete, Relation or join, subquery, ColumnExpr, Group/Having, and typed scan target.

assertions.text: The output includes basic CRUD examples using Bun query builders.
The output includes an advanced query with relation or join, subquery, aggregation, and grouping.
The output uses placeholders for values instead of string-concatenating user input.

evals.prompt: Use the official Bun Guide Migration and Schema Management plus Best Practices chapters to review a plan that creates tables automatically on production startup and sends emails inside db.RunInTx.
evals.expected_output: Recommends explicit Bun migrations/fixtures and transaction best practices; discourages hidden production schema mutation and external side effects inside transactions.

assertions.text: The output recommends explicit migrations using Bun's migration concepts instead of hidden production startup schema mutation.
The output discusses migration locking or explicit migration execution.
The output keeps email or other external side effects outside the transaction boundary.
